Made by D.I. Robertson. Forwarded by Tho Robertson a/D.11.

Sir,
With reference to the attached letter of August 20, 1929
from Mr. A. Fenkl wherein he informs us that he has severed
his connections with the Argus Information and Investigation
Bureau inquiries show that the latter concern closed on August
1, on which date Dr. Robert Brzesowsky left for Japan. At
the end of August 1929 Messrs David Sassoon & Co. Ltd, 23 Kiangse
Road who leased the premises at 33 Kiangse Road to Dr. Robert
Brzesowsky received a letter from the latter, dated Unzen,
Japan August 15, to the effect that he had gone to Japan to
recuperate and incidently found employment as the representative
of two Insurance companies. In his letter he further requested
Messrs David Sassoon & Co. Ltd to relieve him of the lease of
the premises from September 15, and to auction the contents
to meet the arrears of rent. In the event of the money realised
from the sale of the contents being insufficient to cover the
amount due he promised to pay the balance at some future date.
Dr. Robert Brzesowsky's address is the Shinyu Hotel, Unzen,
Nagasaki Ken, Japan.

From information received it appears that the Chinese
authorities refused to subsidize the Argus Information and
Investigation Bureau, probably on the recommendation of Mr.
Alfred de Crosse who did not like the idea of having a rival
to compete with, and in consequence was forced to close down
for lack of funds.

Mr. Fenkl states that he had no quarrel with Dr.
Brzesowsky and as business was very bad he accepted temporary
employment at the Shanghai Water Works from August 1st to August

closure of your Bureau.

May 31st. 1929.

To the
Shanghai Municipal Council
present.

Dear Sirs:-

We have established at Shanghai, No.33 Kiangse
Road 3rd floor, an Inquiry Agency called "ARGUS INFORMATION
& INVESTIGATION BUREAU". It is our intention to conduct
the Business of that concern in accordance with the tradi-
tions of similar bureaux in the large cities of Europe and
the United States. As we in the furtherance of the interests
of our clients, and the Police, in pursuance of their daily
work, will frequently have objects in common, the avoidance
of friction and promotion of co-operation are aims which we
shall always keep before us, and with this end in view we
are now writing to explain to the Municipal Council the
character of our work.

The business of the Argus, Information & Investi-
gation Bureau will comprise enquiries into commercial,
financial and private matters, and efficiency, honesty and
secrecy shall be our watchwords in the discharge of this work.

We shall undertake investigations of matters, in
which official interference is inadvisable through considera-
tion of prestige or family dignity. We shall never act against
the public interest by concealing from the proper authorities
knowledge of any felony or crime of a heinous nature, Cases
of this category coming under notice will be brought without
delay to the attention of the official police authorities, to
whom we shall render every assistance possible to the in
bringing the criminals to justice.

尊敬的先生们：

我们在上海江西路 33 号三楼设立了一家名为“阿尔戈斯信息与调查局”的调查机构。我们打算按照欧洲和美国大城市中类似机构的传统来经营此项业务。由于我们在维护客户利益方面，与警方在日常工作中经常有共同的目标，因此避免摩擦和促进合作是我们始终牢记的目标；为此，我们现在致函向工部局说明我们工作的性质。

阿尔戈斯信息与调查局的业务包括对商业、金融和私人事务进行调查，效率、诚实和保密将是我们在履行此项工作时的座右铭。

我们将承担那些因顾及声望或家庭尊严而不宜由官方介入的事项的调查。我们绝不会通过向主管当局隐瞒任何重罪或恶性犯罪的知识而损害公共利益。此类案件一旦被发现，将立即提请官方警察当局注意，我们将全力协助他们将罪犯绳之以法。

2.

Investigations will be conducted and confidential
reports will be made on behalf of Insurance Companies which
lack the staff requisite to attend to such matters themselves.
We shall not interfere in public affairs, or concern ourselves
in any way with enquiries touching upon political, military
or naval matters.

We have only opened our offices and our staff is
small. We are convinced, however, that Shanghai offers a wide
field for business of the nature we are engaged. Consequently
developments an increase of staff are expected. We realise
that the achievement of the success, for which we hope, will
depend largely on the sympathy extended to us by the official
authorities.

The members of the staff are at present:
Mr. A. Fenkl, formerly in the military secret service
of the Austrian Army.
Dr. R. Brzesowsky, formerly in the Central Police of
the Austrian Government Police Forces.
Mr. Nikola Marinitch, Chief of the White Russian Or-
ganisation and connected with General Horvat at Peking.

We sincerely hope that the foregoing remarks will
satisfy you of the legitimate character of our business, and
the Commissioner of Police will appoint an officer unofficially
to keep in touch with us, so that he will be at all times able
to secure our co-operation and satisfy himself that we are liv-
ing up to our professions.

We trust in conclusion that the Municipal Council will
be so good as to grant any licence or permit which may be re-
quired to enable us to proceed with our business.

Faithfully yours
AROUS
INFORMATION & INVESTIGATION
BUREAU
A. Fenkl,
Dr. R. Brzesowsky

我们将代表那些缺乏必要人员自行处理此类事项的保险公司进行调查并出具机密报告。我们不干涉公共事务，也不以任何方式参与涉及政治、军事或海军事务的调查。

我们刚刚开设办事处，员工人数很少。然而，我们确信上海为我们所从事的这种性质的业务提供了广阔的市场。因此，预计会有发展和人员增加。我们认识到，我们希望取得的成功在很大程度上取决于官方当局给予我们的同情与支持。

目前的员工成员如下：
A. Fenkl 先生，前奥地利军队军事情报部门人员。
R. Brzesowsky 博士，前奥地利政府警察部队中央警察局人员。
Nikola Marinitch 先生，白俄组织负责人，并与北京的霍瓦特将军（General Horvat）有联系。

我们真诚希望上述说明能使你们相信我们业务的合法性，并希望警务处长能非正式地指派一名官员与我们保持联系，以便他随时能够获得我们的合作，并确认我们正在践行我们的承诺。

最后，我们相信工部局会惠予颁发使我们能够开展业务所需的任何执照或许可证。

忠实于你们的

CONFIDENTIAL. REPORT
Date June 5, 1929

Subject (in full) Argus Information and Intelligence Bureau.

Made by D. I. Robertson. Forwarded by （签名：Thos Robertson C.D.I.）

The Argus Information and Intelligence Bureau is
situated on the 3rd floor of 33 Kiangse Road in premises
rented from Messrs David Sassoon and Coy at $160.00 per mensem.
The tenancy of the premises was taken over by Dr. Robert
Brzesowsky M.D. from the landlords on February 1, 1929, and
the tenant gave as guarantee a letter of recommendation from
the local Czecho-Slovakian Consul. Two signboards are
exhibited outside the main entrance one of which reads in
English "Dr. Med. B. Robert" and the other "Dr. Robert
Brzesowsky M.D." while each board bears the inscription in
Chinese "Specialist in Venereal Diseases, Skin Diseases and
Gonorrhea". The official card of the Bureau bears the words
in English on one side "Argus Information and Intelligence
Bureau, Office 33 Kiangse Road, Tel. 18927". On the reverse
side, a translation of the English inscription appears and in
addition the two Chinese characters 偵緝 , a translation
of which means "to spy" and "to search for in order to arrest"
and can, therefore, be interpreted only that the Bureau possess
power of arrest. The proprietors are Dr. Robert Brzesowsky
and Dr. Van Kristner. The foreign assistants are Kedrelivansky,
Fenki and Marinetch, while several Chinese agents are also
employed.

In spite of assurances from Dr. Brzesowsky that the
bureau is purely commercial and non-political it is almost

either the National Government or some group of Government
Kuomintang officials. In confirmation of this suspicion,

阿尔戈斯信息与情报局位于江西路 33 号三楼，房屋系从大卫·沙逊公司（Messrs David Sassoon and Coy）租用，月租金为 160.00 美元。该房屋的租约由罗伯特·布热佐夫斯基医学博士（Dr. Robert Brzesowsky M.D.）于 1929 年 2 月 1 日从房东处接手，租户提供的担保是一封来自当地捷克斯洛伐克领事的推荐信。主入口外悬挂两块招牌，一块用英文写着“Dr. Med. B. Robert”，另一块写着“Dr. Robert Brzesowsky M.D.”，每块牌子上均有中文 inscription “花柳皮肤淋病专科”。该局的官方名片正面印有英文“Argus Information and Intelligence Bureau, Office 33 Kiangse Road, Tel. 18927”。背面是英文内容的翻译，此外还有两个汉字“偵緝”，其翻译意为“间谍”和“搜查以逮捕”，因此只能解释为该局拥有逮捕权。所有者为罗伯特·布热佐夫斯基博士和范·克里斯特纳博士（Dr. Van Kristner）。外籍助手有 Kedrelivansky、Fenki 和 Marinetch，同时还雇佣了几名中国线人。

Dr. Gustav Ritter Von Krietner L.L.D., M.D. is an
Austrian citizen and for some years prior to the Great War
his father served as Consul-General for Austria in Yokohama.

In 1911 Dr. von Krietner was engaged by the Peking
Head Officer of the Chinese Maritime Customs and stationed
at Foochow where he served under the local Commissioner of
Customs Herr Von Tanner as 4th Assistant "C". In March 1913
he resigned and the Customs records show that he "left without
permission", i.e. that he was a bad character. He then
returned to Austria and saw service in the Great War.

At the end of 1927 he was employed as Advisor to
the Police Department at Canton. In 1928 he was to be
appointed as Advisor to the Chekiang Public Safety Department
to assist in the formation of a Secret Police Political
Service, but owing to the recent trouble with Kuangsi the
appointment was never confirmed. He then sought the
assistance of his great friend, the late Col. Max Bauer,
who presented him to various Nanking Government officials
with whom he is still in touch.

It is reported that Von Krietner knew Dr. Krassovsky's
father when the latter was in the Vienna Police, hence the
friendship between the two men in Shanghai.

In answer to a telephonic request, I visited at
noon to-day Dr. R. Brezovsky at his office at No. 33 Kiamgu
Road and was informed by him that subject to permission being
given by the Municipal Police, he would open an information
bureau entitled "Argus" Information & Investigation Bureau
at his present address. He states that this is a small
venture, having but little capital, but considers it would
fill out a long felt want. The staff at present consists
of the following persons :-
1. Dr. Brezovsky
2. Mr. Denki
3. Mr. Kedrelivansky
4. Mr. Burinsteh

At the inception of the Bureau the staff will not receive
salaries. In fact, it raised the initial expenses of $25.00
per person. A plan of the Bureau's proposed activities,
which Dr. R. Brezovsky has drawn up for the information of
the Municipal Police is attached.

He further informed me that at 6.00 p.m. May 14 and on
May 16, Alfred de Groot visited him and made enquiries with
regard to this proposed bureau. De Groot stated that he
was sent by General Chiang Kai-shek to make enquiries about
this bureau as it was suspected to be the local office of the
Communist (Soviet) Secret Service, that they were taking
measures to have something like this put down and that the General
would take steps against him if he continued to carry on.
Subsequently, however, he stated that he did not intend to do
so unless he was asked to do so by any head of authority.

are not intended as: theft among relations of the same
family or other similar affairs,when the esteem and the good
name of the family should be taken care and official
prosecution is not wanted by the family.

Confidential reports,investigations and informations as req
quested by the Insurance Offices,which are not sufficient
supplied with own investigation officers.

As a rule cases of a nature where official police prosecution
is necessary,will not be accepted and the parties concerned
will be advised to bring such cases before the official
police forces.Besides the police forces will be informed
about such cases from our office immediately.

On the other hand our office will give any informations
requested by the Police force as far as our office should
be able to do so if connected with such cases.

The Police Department is kindly requested by our office,
inofficially to appoint one of his representatives to act as mediator
between the Police Department and our office in order to
be always informed of the business-actions conducted by
our office and the correct and honest conduct of the same.

As at the present our office is only at the start naturally
the staff of the office is a small one but as we are con-
vinced that Shanghai has a similar field of work
for such an office as all Cities in Europe the members of
the staff shall be increased accordingly to the need,
and we shall be much obliged to the Police Forces in
obtaining of the kindly favour of them.

CONFIDENTIAL.
June 8, 29
Argus Information and Intelligence Bureau.

SECRET & CONFIDENTIAL

The Argus Information and Intelligence Bureau is
situated on the 3rd floor of 33 Kiangsu Road in premises
rented from Messrs David Sassoon and Coy at Tls. . . per month.
The tenancy of the premises was taken over by Dr. Robert
Krasnovsky A.M. from the landlords on February 1, 1929, and
the tenant gave as guarantee a letter of recommendation from
the local Czecho-Slovakian Consul. Two signboards are
exhibited outside the main entrance one of which reads in
English "Dr. Med. R. Robert" and the other "Dr. Robert
Krasnovsky M.D." while each board bears the inscription in
Chinese "Specialist in Venereal Diseases, Skin Diseases and
Gonorrhoea". The official card of the Bureau bears the words
in English on one side "Argus Information and Intelligence
Bureau, Office 33 Kiangsu Road, Tel. 5067". On the reverse
side, a translation of the English inscription appears and in
addition the two Chinese characters 偵緝 , a translation
of which means "to spy" and "to search for in order to arrest"
and can, therefore, be interpreted only that the Bureau possesses
power of arrest. The proprietors are Dr. Robert Krasnovsky
and Mr. Van Kristner. The foreign assistants are Krasniltzky,
David and Marinitch, while several Chinese agents are also
employed.

In spite of assurances from Dr. Krasnovsky that the
Bureau is purely commercial and non-political it is almost
positive that it is a political organisation established by
either the National Government or some group of disaffected
militarists. In confirmation of this suspicion,
information has been received that Dr. Krasnovsky claims to
have connections with all the leading political parties.

秘密与机密

阿尔戈斯情报与信息事务所位于江苏路33号三楼，房屋系从沙逊洋行（Messrs David Sassoon and Coy）租用，月租金为台币...元。该房屋的租赁权由 Robert Krasnovsky 医学博士（A.M.）于1929年2月1日从房东处承接，租户提供了一份当地捷克斯洛伐克领事的推荐信作为担保。主入口外悬挂两块招牌，一块用英文写着“Dr. Med. R. Robert”（R. Robert 医学博士），另一块写着“Dr. Robert Krasnovsky M.D.”（Robert Krasnovsky 医学博士），每块招牌上均有中文题字“花柳皮肤淋病专科”。该事务所的官方名片一面印有英文“Argus Information and Intelligence Bureau, Office 33 Kiangsu Road, Tel. 5067”（阿尔戈斯情报与信息事务所，江苏路33号，电话5067）。背面是英文内容的译文，此外还有两个汉字“偵緝”，其翻译意为“间谍”和“搜捕”，因此只能解释为该事务所拥有逮捕权。业主为 Robert Krasnovsky 博士和 Van Kristner 先生。外籍助手有 Krasniltzky、David 和 Marinitch，同时还雇佣了几名华籍探员。

尽管 Krasnovsky 博士保证该事务所纯属商业性质且非政治性，但几乎可以肯定它是一个由国民政府或某些不满的军阀集团建立的政治组织。证实这一怀疑的是，收到消息称 Krasnovsky 博士声称与所有主要政党都有联系。

In consequence of the latter information, an informer

The following is a brief summary of the antecedents

Dr. Kressevsky is the son of a Russian

鉴于上述信息，5月11日派遣了一名线人向 Kressevsky 博士申请担任情报探员的职位，后者告知该线人，在该事务所从南京政府获得必要资金之前，无法考虑其雇佣事宜。然而，他承诺一旦收到预期资金，将以每月800.00美元的薪水外加所有刑事案件10%的佣金雇佣该线人从事政治和刑事情报工作。Kressevsky 博士还告诉线人，Von Kribotner 博士正在努力筹集资金，一旦事务所开始运作，将在中国各省雇佣外籍和华籍探员收集政治情报，并通过该事务所转交给南京政府。关于这后一种说法，值得注意的是，Von Kribotner 博士于5月15日前往南京，据报道他正通过苏联顾问团对南京政府施加影响。

以下是 Kressevsky 博士和 Von Kribotner 博士的简要背景摘要，涵盖他们此前与南京政府的关系以及该情报局的情况。

Dr. Gustav Ritter von Kriechner L.L.D., Ph.D. is an
Austrian citizen and for some years prior to the Great War
his father served as Consul-General for Austria in Yokohama.
In 1911 Dr. Von Kriechner was engaged by the Peking
Head Office of the Chinese Maritime Customs and stationed
at Foochow where he served under the local Commissioner of
Customs Herr Von Taussig as 4th Assistant "C". In March 1913
he resigned and the Customs records show that he "left without
permission", i.e. that he was a bad character. He then
returned to Austria and saw service in the Great War.
At the end of 1927 he was employed as Advisor to
the Police Department at Canton. In 1928 he was to be
appointed as Adviser to the Chekiang Public Safety Department
to assist in the formation of a Secret Police Political
Service, but owing to the recent trouble with Kwangsi the
appointment was never confirmed. He then sought the
assistance of his great friend, the late Col. Max Bauer,
who presented him to various Nanking Government officials
with whom he is still in touch.
It is reported that Von Kriechner knew Mr. Brzozowsky's
father when the latter was in the Vienna Police, hence the
friendship between the two men in Shanghai.

Gustav Ritter von Kriechner 法学博士、哲学博士是一位奥地利公民，大战前数年，他的父亲曾担任奥地利驻横滨总领事。1911年，Von Kriechner 博士受聘于中国海关北京总税务司署，派驻福州，在当地税务司 Von Taussig 先生手下担任第四助理“C”级职员。1913年3月，他辞职，海关记录显示他“未经许可离开”，即他是一个品行不端的人。随后他返回奥地利，并在大战中服役。
1927年底，他被聘为广州警务处顾问。1928年，他本将被任命为浙江省公安厅顾问，协助组建秘密警察政治服务机构，但由于近期与广西方面的纠纷，该任命从未得到确认。随后他寻求其挚友、已故 Max Bauer 上校的帮助，后者将他引荐给多位南京政府官员，他至今仍与这些人保持联系。
据报道，Von Kriechner 认识 Brzozowsky 先生的父亲，当时后者在维也纳警察局任职，因此这两人在上海建立了友谊。
Alois Funkl，1886年11月17日出生于捷克斯洛伐克埃格尔地区的法尔肯瑙，德意志国籍，捷克斯洛伐克臣民。从皮尔森国立技术学院机械工程专业毕业后，他

he was appointed Chief of the Military Secret Service of the
77th Regiment of the Austrian Army and in October 1918 was
captured on the Russian frontier and sent to Blagoveshchensk.
In 1917 he was released for employment and after the first
Russian revolution fled to Irkutsk, where he was imprisoned

Army he was released and obtained employment in Tarbagatai,

In Harbin he was engaged as a technical agent by
the International Sleeping Car Company for about one year
at the end of which time he secured a post with Hugo Stinnes

In 1923 he entered the service of Buchmeister & Co., 8 Siking

held until January 8, 1926. He was then unemployed until
he became interested in the Argus Information and Intelligence

在哈尔滨，他为国际卧铺车公司（International Sleeping Car Company）担任技术代理约一年，期满后在上海的胡戈·施廷内斯中国公司（Hugo Stinnes China Co.）谋得职位，后调至其青岛分公司。1923年，他进入四川路8号布赫迈斯特公司（Buchmeister & Co.）任职，并于1924年被任命为经理，该职位他一直担任至1926年1月8日。此后他一直失业，直到对阿耳戈斯情报与信息局（Argus Information and Intelligence Bureau）产生兴趣。

Vladimir Kedrolivansky was born in 1893 and is a
White Russian. On December 3, 1923 he was appointed Temporary
Constable in the Shanghai Municipal Police and attached to
Hongkew Station. On May 1, 1925 he was transferred to the
Criminal Investigation Department and on July 7, 1926
transferred to the Intelligence Office, in which department
he remained until he was permitted to terminate his services
as sergeant on November 1, 1927. On leaving the Municipal
Police he was appointed Russian intelligence officer to
Marshal Chang Hsun Chang's army and stationed in the Special
Area at Tientsin. After the fall of the latter warlord
in 1928 he proceeded to Tsingtao, where for a time he was
employed as an intelligence agent for Japanese interests. In
November 1928 he returned to Shanghai, where he continued to
work for Japanese interests, but discontinued these
activities to enter the employment of the Argus Information
and Intelligence Bureau.

A German gonorrhoea specialist, in the Shun Pao dated

I have recently arrived in Shanghai from Germany
and have established an office at no.33 Kiangse Road,
South of Nanking Road. I am fully experienced in
venereal, skin and other diseases, especially gonorrhoea.
Very often gonorrhoea cannot be eradicated because the
patients were negligent at the first stage or they have
had no adequate medical treatment. I conducted
researches for over ten years in the St Larl (?) Hospital,
Germany, and have discovered the most up-to-date treatment
and can therefore tell for certainty, upon examination,
whether a patient has been suffering from gonorrhoea
for a long time or otherwise. If a patient is
completely cured, he can secure a testimonial from
the Municipal Laboratory to show that he has been
completely cured. In order to extend German medical
knowledge, the charges for medical attendance are
moderate. An interpreter is provided.
Patients may have a trial.
Office hours:- From 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.
No office on Sunday.

June 9, 29

CONFIDENTIAL.

Argus Information and Intelligence Bureau.

SECRET & CONFIDENTIAL

The Argus Information and Intelligence Bureau is
situated on the 3rd floor of 33 Kiangsu Road in premises
rented from Messrs David Sassoon and Coy at Tls. 100.00 per mensem.
The tenancy of the premises was taken over by Dr. Robert
Brasovsky M.D. from the landlords on February 1, 1929, and
the tenant gave as guarantee a letter of recommendation from
the local Czecho-Slovakian Consul. Two signboards are
exhibited outside the main entrance one of which reads in
English "Dr. Med. R. Robert" and the other "Dr. Robert
Brasovsky M.D." while each board bears the inscription in
Chinese "Specialist in Venereal Diseases, Skin Diseases and
Gonorrhoea". The official card of the Bureau bears the words
in English on one side "Argus Information and Intelligence
Bureau, Office 33 Kiangsu Road, Tel. 18927". On the reverse
side, a translation of the English inscription appears and in
addition the two Chinese characters 偵緝 , a translation
of which means "to spy" and "to search for in order to arrest"
and can, therefore, be interpreted only that the Bureau possess
power of arrest. The proprietors are Dr. Robert Brasovsky
and Dr. Van Erietner. The foreign assistants are Fedrolivensky,
Fenkl and Karinstein, while several Chinese agents are also
employed.

In spite of assurances from Dr. Brasovsky that the
bureau is purely commercial and non-political it is almost
positive that it is a political organisation subsidised by
either the National Government or some group of Government
Nanking officials. In confirmation of this suspicion,
information has been received that Mr. Brasovsky prior to
establishing himself at 33 Kiangsu Road approached General

阿耳戈斯情报与信息局。

秘密且机密

阿耳戈斯情报与信息局位于江苏路33号三楼，房屋系从沙逊洋行（Messrs David Sassoon and Coy）租用，月租金为100两。该房屋的租赁权由罗伯特·布拉斯科夫斯基医学博士（Dr. Robert Brasovsky M.D.）于1929年2月1日从房东处承接，租户提供的担保是一封来自当地捷克斯洛伐克领事的推荐信。正门外悬挂两块招牌，一块用英文写着“Dr. Med. R. Robert”，另一块写着“Dr. Robert Brasovsky M.D.”，每块招牌上均有中文 inscription “性病、皮肤病及淋病专家”。该局的名片正面印有英文“Argus Information and Intelligence Bureau, Office 33 Kiangsu Road, Tel. 18927”。背面是英文内容的译文，此外还有两个汉字“偵緝”，其翻译意为“侦察”和“搜捕”，因此只能解释为该局拥有逮捕权。业主为罗伯特·布拉斯科夫斯基博士和范·埃里特纳博士（Dr. Van Erietner）。外籍助手有费德罗利文斯基（Fedrolivensky）、芬克尔（Fenkl）和卡林斯坦（Karinstein），同时还雇佣了几名华籍探员。

尽管布拉斯科夫斯基博士保证该局纯属商业性质且非政治性，但几乎可以肯定它是一个政治组织，由国民政府或南京政府某派官员资助。证实这一怀疑的情报显示，布拉斯科夫斯基先生在江苏路33号立足之前，曾向蒋

page_data.en:

Chiang Kai shek for a subsidy of $3,000.00 per month.
This sum was officially refused but owing to the present
uncertain state of the political situation it is suspected that
Chiang Kai Shek issued the subsidy secretly as it is reported
he has several such confidential organizations working on his
behalf.

In consequence of the latter information, an informer
was sent on May 11 to make application to Dr. Brzesowsky for
a position as an intelligence agent and was informed by the
latter that until the bureau received the necessary funds
from the Nanking Government his employment could not be
considered. He, however, promised to employ the informer on
political and criminal intelligence work as soon as the
expected funds were received at a salary of $200.00 per
month plus 10% commission on all criminal cases. Dr. Brzesowsky
also told the informer that Dr. Von Kristner was trying to
get the money and once the bureau was in working order, foreign
and Chinese agents would be employed in various provinces in
China to gather political intelligence for transmission through
the bureau to the Nanking Government. In connection with
this latter statement it is significant that Dr. Von Kristner
left for Nanking on May 13 and is reported to be using his
influences, through the senior group of advisers, with the
Nanking Government.

The following is a brief summary of the antecedents
of Drs. Brzesowsky and von Kristner, showing their previous
connection with the Nanking Government, and of the assistants
employed.

Dr. Robert Brzesowsky is the son of a former high
page_data.zh:
- 8 -
介石将军申请每月3,000美元的津贴。这笔款项被正式拒绝，但由于目前政治局势不明朗，怀疑蒋介石秘密发放了该津贴，因为有报告称他有数个此类机密组织为其效力。

鉴于上述情报，5月11日派遣一名线人向布热佐夫斯基博士（Dr. Brzesowsky）申请情报特工职位，后者告知线人，在该局收到南京政府的必要资金之前，无法考虑其雇佣事宜。然而，他承诺一旦收到预期资金，将以月薪200美元外加所有刑事案件10%佣金的条件雇佣该线人从事政治和刑事情报工作。布热佐夫斯基博士还告诉线人，冯·克里斯特纳博士（Dr. Von Kristner）正在努力筹措资金，一旦该局开始运作，将在中国各省雇佣外籍和华籍特工收集政治情报，并通过该局传递给南京政府。关于这后一种说法，值得注意的是，冯·克里斯特纳博士于5月13日前往南京，据报道他正通过高级顾问团对南京政府施加影响。

以下是布热佐夫斯基博士和冯·克里斯特纳博士及其所雇助手的背景简要总结，显示他们此前与南京政府的关系。

罗伯特·布热佐夫斯基博士是一位前高级

police official in Vienna and obtained his medical diploma
in Prague. He was born at Brünn, Austria, in 1884 and in
1904 served one year's voluntary military service. From
1905 to 1909 he served in the Austrian Army and in the latter
year graduated from the Military University. In 1910 he
entered Austrian Government service with special duties
in the Government Police Forces. From 1914 to 1918 he saw
service in the Great War with the Austrian Army on the
borders of Russia and Albania. He is registered at the local
Czecho Slovakian Consulate. About four years ago Dr. Robert
Krossowsky was appointed Medical Advisor to the Headquarters
of the Nationalist Army and still exhibits a certificate,
signed by Tang Ching Wei and Chiang Kai Shek, to that effect
in one of the rooms at 53 Kiangse Road. He has resided in
Shanghai at different periods within the last three years.
Early in 1926, he opened a hospital at 98 Rue Massenet with
funds alleged to have been received from the Bolsheviks,
but was forced to close down owing to financial difficulties.
In the same year, he visited Europe, travelling via Siberia,
for ten months and shortly after his return to Shanghai in
1927 visited Mukden on two occasions. It was observed that
on his return from these visits he was in possession of ample
funds. Sometime after his visit to Mukden, he opened a
Medical Cabinet at 80 Museum Road and a watch maintained
over the premises for a month disclosed the fact that no
patients ever visited him. It is also reported that at
one time he acted as Medical Adviser to the late Soviet
Consulate.
In this connection it is important that Dr.Krossowsky's

维也纳警察官员的儿子，并在布拉格获得医学文凭。他1884年出生于奥地利布尔诺（Brünn），1904年服役一年志愿兵役。1905年至1909年在奥地利陆军服役，并于同年从军事大学毕业。1910年，他进入奥地利政府部门服役，在政府警察部队中担任特殊职务。1914年至1918年，他在大战期间随奥地利陆军在俄罗斯和阿尔巴尼亚边境服役。他在当地捷克斯洛伐克领事馆注册。大约四年前，罗伯特·克罗索夫斯基博士（Dr. Robert Krossowsky）被任命为国民革命军总司令部的医学顾问，至今仍在江西路53号的一个房间内展示一张由唐精卫（Tang Ching Wei，音译）和蒋介石签署的证明证书。在过去三年中，他曾不同时期居住在上海。1926年初，他用据称来自布尔什维克的资金在马思南路98号开设了一家医院，但因财务困难被迫关闭。同年，他经西伯利亚前往欧洲旅行十个月，1927年回到上海后不久，两次访问沈阳。据观察，他从这些访问回来时拥有充裕的资金。访问沈阳后不久，他在博物院路80号开设了一家医务室，对该处所进行一个月的监视后发现，从未有病人来访。另有报告称，他曾一度担任前苏联领事馆的医学顾问。

Dr. Gustav Ritter Von Krietner l.l..o, b. . 18 ..
austrian citizen and for some years prior to the great war
his father served as consul-general for austria in yokohama.
in 1911 dr. von krietner was engaged by the chinese
head officer of the chinese maritime customs and stationed
at foochow where he served under the local commissioner of
customs herr von tauner as 4th assistant "c". in march 1913
he resigned and the customs records show that he "left without
permission", i.e. that he was a bad character. he then
returned to austria and saw service in the great war.
at the end of 1927 he was employed as advisor to
the police department at canton. in 1928 he was to be
appointed as adviser to the chekiang public safety department
to assist in the formation of a secret police political
service, but owing to the recent trouble with kwangsi the
appointment was never confirmed. he then sought the
assistance of his great friend, the late col. max sauer,
who presented him to various nanking government officials
with whom he is still in touch.
it is reported that von krietner knew dr. krzizewsky's
father when the latter was in the vienna police, hence the
friendship between the two men in shanghai.
alexis penzl, born november 17, 1898 at falkenau ,

前合伙人，一位名叫安东·欧勒（Anton Euler）的奥地利人，也受雇于国民党军队，1927年在上海因奉鲍罗廷（Borodin）之命与敌人交易而被枪决。
古斯塔夫·里特尔·冯·克里特纳博士（Dr. Gustav Ritter Von Krietner），L.L.O.，生于18..年，奥地利公民，大战前数年，其父曾任奥地利驻横滨总领事。1911年，冯·克里特纳博士受雇于中国海关华方总税务司，驻扎福州，在当地税务司陶纳尔先生（Herr von Tauner）手下担任第四助理“C”级。1913年3月辞职，海关记录显示他“未经许可离开”，即品行不端。随后他返回奥地利，并在大战中服役。
1927年底，他被聘为广州警察局顾问。1928年，他本将被任命为浙江省公安厅顾问，协助组建秘密警察政治服务机构，但因最近与广西方面的纠纷，该任命从未得到确认。随后他寻求其挚友、已故的马克斯·绍尔上校（Col. Max Sauer）的帮助，后者将他引荐给多位南京政府官员，他至今仍与这些人保持联系。
据报道，冯·克里特纳在克里热夫斯基博士（Dr. Krzizewsky，音译）的父亲任职维也纳警察时便认识他，因此两人在上海建立了友谊。
亚历克西斯·彭茨尔（Alexis Penzl），1898年11月17日出生于捷克斯洛伐克埃格尔的法尔肯瑙（Falkenau, Eger），具有德国国籍，是捷克斯洛伐克臣民。从皮尔森（Pilsen）的国立技术学院机械工程专业毕业后，他

engaged until March 1915 with the own construction department
of theroda Works in the same city. Shortly afterwards
he was appointed Chief of the Military Secret Service of the
70th Regiment of the Austrian Army and in October 1916 was
captured on the Russian frontier and sent to Blagoveschensk.
In 1917 he was released for employment and after the first
Russian revolution fled to Irkutsk, where he was imprisoned
by the Red Army. On the recapture of Irkutsk by the White
Army he was released and obtained employment in Tarbagatai,
Transbaikal, until December 1920, when he was forced to escape
to Harbin on his being suspected of conspiracy with the
White Russian Army against the Bolsheviks.
In Harbin he was engaged as a technical agent by
the International Sleeping Car Company for about one year
at the end of which time he secured a post with Hugo Stinnes
China Co., in Shanghai and later at their branch at Tsingtao.
In 1933 he entered the service of Archheister & Co., 8 Nanking
Road, and in 1934 was appointed manager, which position he
held until January 8, 1936. He was then unemployed until
he became interested in the Argus Information and Intelligence
Bureau.

Constable in the Shanghai Municipal Police and attached to
Hongkew Station. On May 1, 1925 he was transferred to the

transferred to the Intelligence Office, in which department
he remained until he was permitted to terminate his services
as sergeant on November 1, 1927. On leaving the Municipal

Area at Tientsin. After the fall of the latter warlord
in 1928 he proceeded to Tsingtao, where for a time he was
employed as an Intelligence agent for Japanese interests. In
November 1928 he returned to Shanghai, where he continued to
work for Japanese interests, but discontinued these
activities to enter the employment of the Argus Information
and Intelligence Bureau.

Made by D.I. Robertson Forwarded by Tho Robertson, C.D.I.
In accordance with your instructions I interviewed
Dr. R. Brzesowsky of the Argus Information and Investigation
Bureau at 33 Kiangse Road on June 8 when he reiterated the
contents of his letter of May 31, 1929, addressed to the
Shanghai Municipal Council.
In addition Dr. Brzesowsky stated that the Bureau
would commence operations as soon as permission was received
from the Council. He stated that the Bureau has no funds and
that neither he, Mr. Jenkl nor Mr. Marinetch receive any
salary. He also denied that Kedrolivansky is working for
them adding that he is unable to pay him the wages he asked.
Dr. Brzesowsky moreover stated that he was unable, through
lack of capital, to engage any assistants and, in the event
of permission being granted to open the Bureau, all inquiries
would be made by Jenkl, Marinetch and himself until such
times as he was in a position to employ outside labour. When
questioned regarding the two Chinese characters on the Bureau's
official cards (referred to in my report of June 6) Dr.
Brzesowsky stated that the characters were wrong and that new
cards were now being printed from which the characters in
question would be eliminated.
